# `starhermit:physics`

Engine **1.41.0** (host API 1.41), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:physics";
```

The engine's 3D rigid-body world (since API\_MINOR 40; older games cannot import it; spec/physics-and-particles.html). It runs natively in the engine (starhermit-physics-3d), and the same code, compiled to WebAssembly, runs it in browsers: with only IEEE 754 basic operations and the engine's own math functions, the same calls give bit-identical worlds on every platform, so lockstep multiplayer games can step it. An engine extension: three.js has no physics.

Units are metres, kilograms and seconds; +Y is up by convention only (gravity and the character controller's `up` say which way). Every position and translation must be within 1,000,000 m of the origin on each axis, speeds, forces and impulses within 1e9: anything else, and any NaN, throws a RangeError before the world changes. Native work is charged to the call's fuel in proportion to what it did.

Step the world from onFixedUpdate and place objects from onRender:

```text
const world = new PhysicsWorld();
world.createCollider({ shape: { type: "trimesh", geometry: level.geometry } });
const crate = world.createBody({ position: [0, 5, 0], object: crateMesh });
world.createCollider({ shape: { type: "box", halfExtents: [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] } }, crate);
onFixedUpdate((dt) => world.step(dt));
onRender((alpha) => world.sync(alpha));
```

### ShapeDesc

*type*

```ts
export type ShapeDesc =
  | { type: "sphere"; radius: number }
  | { type: "box"; halfExtents: VectorLike }
  | { type: "capsule"; halfHeight: number; radius: number }
  | { type: "cylinder" | "cone"; halfHeight: number; radius: number; segments?: number }
  | { type: "convexHull"; points?: ArrayLike<number>; geometry?: GeometryLike; scale?: VectorLike }
  | {
      type: "trimesh";
      vertices?: ArrayLike<number>;
      indices?: ArrayLike<number> | null;
      geometry?: GeometryLike;
      scale?: VectorLike;
    }
  | { type: "heightfield"; rows: number; columns: number; heights: ArrayLike<number>; size: { x: number; z: number } }
  | { type: "plane" }
  | { type: "triangle"; a: VectorLike; b: VectorLike; c: VectorLike };
```

A shape's description. Convex shapes (sphere, box, capsule, cylinder, cone, convexHull, triangle) go on any body and in casts and overlaps; trimesh, heightfield and plane only on static or kinematic bodies, and they collide with convex shapes (not with each other).

- `capsule`: a segment of `halfHeight` each way along local Y, rounded by `radius`.
- `cylinder`, `cone`: hulls of `segments` (3 to 128, default 24) points round local Y, `halfHeight` each way (a cone's apex at +halfHeight).
- `convexHull`: the hull of `points` (x, y, z triples) or of a geometry's vertices, optionally `scale`d; at most 512 points feed it, those furthest out along 256 directions first (up to 1,048,576 in).
- `trimesh`: two-sided triangles from `vertices` and `indices` (none: each three vertices a triangle) or a geometry; equal positions are welded, triangles without area dropped, and edges between nearly coplanar triangles are smoothed so things slide across seams. Up to 1,048,576 vertices and triangles.
- `heightfield`: `rows` x `columns` heights (row by row, rows along Z), spanning `size` centred on the collider (2 to 16,384 a side, at most 4,194,304 heights); each cell split from its (column, row) corner to (column + 1, row + 1); solid below its surface.
- `plane`: the half-space below the collider's local XZ plane.
- `triangle`: one two-sided triangle.

```

- `shape: Shape | ShapeDesc;`

### JointType

*type*

```ts
export type JointType = "fixed" | "ball" | "hinge" | "slider" | "distance" | "rope" | "spring" | "coneTwist";
```

- fixed: the bodies keep their relative pose.
- ball: the anchors meet; rotation is free.
- hinge: rotation only about `axis` (in A's frame; default Z), with optional `limits` (radians within ±π) and `motor`.
- slider: B's anchor moves along `axis` (default X) only, rotation locked; `limits` in metres, `motor`.
- distance: the anchors stay `length` apart.
- rope: between `minLength` (default 0) and `maxLength`.
- spring: soft toward `length`, `frequency` Hz (default 2), `dampingRatio` (default 0.5).
- coneTwist: a ball whose `axis` (default Y) stays within `swing` radians and twists within `twist` (default ±π).

  One fixed step of `seconds` (default `timestep`; more than 0, at most 0.1). Call it from onFixedUpdate.

  The last step's touches that began and ended.

  Joints the last step broke (and removed).

- `castRay(from: VectorLike, to: VectorLike, filter?: QueryFilter): RayHit | null;`

- ```ts
  castShape(
      shape: Shape | ShapeDesc,
      position: VectorLike,
      quaternion: QuaternionLike | null | undefined,
      translation: VectorLike,
      filter?: QueryFilter,
    ): ShapeHit | null;
  ```

  A convex shape moved by `translation` from a pose.

- ```ts
  intersectShape(
      shape: Shape | ShapeDesc,
      position: VectorLike,
      quaternion?: QuaternionLike | null,
      filter?: QueryFilter,
    ): Collider[];
  ```

  The colliders a convex shape at a pose overlaps, in creation order.

- `createCharacterController(options?: CharacterOptions): CharacterController;`

- `sync(alpha?: number): void;`

  Places every body's `object` at its pose `alpha` (0 to 1, default 1) of the way through the last step: pass onRender's interpolation for motion that is smooth at any frame rate.

- `dispose(): void;`

  Releases it now: every member of it throws afterwards.

### CharacterOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface CharacterOptions { … }
```

- `up?: VectorLike;`

  Default (0, 1, 0).

- `offset?: number;`

  The gap kept from everything (default 0.02 m, at most 1).

- `slide?: boolean;`

  Slide along what it hits (default true).

- `maxSlopeClimbAngle?: number;`

  Radians: the steepest slope walked up (default π/4).

- `minSlopeSlideAngle?: number;`

  Radians: slopes gentler than this hold it still (default 50°).

- `autostep?: { maxHeight?: number; minWidth?: number; includeDynamicBodies?: boolean } | null;`

  Steps up ledges up to `maxHeight` (default 0.35 m) with at least `minWidth` (default 0.1 m) on top; null turns it off.

- `snapToGround?: number | null;`

  Down to the ground it walked off, this far (default 0.2 m); null turns it off.

- `pushMass?: number | null;`

  Kilograms: pushes dynamic bodies it walks into (default null: they only block it).

- `maxIterations?: number;`

  Hits one move slides off at most (1 to 32, default 8).

### CharacterController

*class*

A kinematic character controller (as Rapier's, which Solstice uses): moves a convex collider through the world, keeping `offset` from everything, sliding along walls, climbing slopes and steps, snapping to the ground, optionally pushing dynamic bodies. The game keeps its own vertical speed (gravity, jumps) and passes the step's motion.

```ts
export class CharacterController { … }
```

- `private constructor();`
- `readonly world: PhysicsWorld;`
- `up: Vec3;`
- `offset: number;`
- `slide: boolean;`
- `maxSlopeClimbAngle: number;`
- `minSlopeSlideAngle: number;`
- `autostep: { maxHeight: number; minWidth: number; includeDynamicBodies: boolean } | null;`
- `snapToGround: number | null;`
- `pushMass: number | null;`
- `maxIterations: number;`

- ```ts
  move(
      collider: Collider,
      desired: VectorLike,
      options?: { filter?: QueryFilter; seconds?: number; apply?: boolean },
    ): CharacterMove;
  ```

  The move `desired` (metres this step) allows; a kinematic body's next pose follows it unless `apply` is false. `seconds` (default the world's timestep) sets pushes' speeds.
